newsitem.title: FRANCE: Long-haul routes plannned for AOM Express.
newsitem.headline: Long-haul routes plannned for AOM Express.

text.p: AOM France Airlines said it planned to extend its airport-to-airport express cargo service to long-haul routes, effective September 1997.

"We launched the service, AOM Express, on our domestic routes from Paris/Orly - Nice, Marseilles, Toulon and Perpignan in November 1996 and have seem steady growth since then," the French carrier's cargo director, Bernard Tetu, told Reuters.
He said the service had performed particularly well on its Paris-Nice and Paris-Marseilles routes as AOM has 11 daily flights to both cities.
"The frequency of our daily departures is a big advantage and for shipments deposited late evening there is the possibility of despatch on early morning flights the next day."
Over the past fortnight, AOM had been testing the express service on its long-haul flights to the French West Indies and Reunion in the Indian Ocean, Tetu added.
"We operate daily frequencies to those destinations so there is real scope for a time-definite service with shipment weights going up to 200 to 300 kilos."
AOM long-haul destinations also include Cayenne French Guyana), Havana, Los Angeles, Tahiti, Colombo, Sydney and New Caledonia.
The airline operates a fleet of 13 Mcdonnell Douglas DC-10s on its long haul network and 11 MD-83s on its domestic network. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
